source: Fourth, our most granular analyses used 3 min time windows. However, for many of the cage sensors, the data are acquired every second. This provides the opportunity for more sophisticated time series analyses that track individual behaviors and rapid fluctuations in physiology.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a potential future direction.

claim: Changes with age occur at all levels of biological organization (molecules, cells, tissues, etc.).
source: Changes with age occur at all levels of biological organization (molecules, cells, tissues, etc.).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as background knowledge.

claim: The study chose to focus on physiology and behavior because changes to this level of biological organization are most proximal to changes in health and quality of life.
source: We chose to focus on physiology and behavior because changes to this level of biological organization are most proximal to changes in health and quality of life.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section explaining the focus of the study.

claim: The system provides advances that allow organism-level aging to be studied with improved throughput, resolution, and physiological scope while reducing the activation energy that comes with highly specialized assay procedures.
source: We created a platform that can measure physiological and behavioral aging at any stage of life in outbred mice using automated phenotyping. This system provides a number of advances that allow organism-level aging to be studied with improved throughput, resolution, and physiological scope while reducing the activation energy that comes with highly specialized assay procedures.

source: Mice were profiled in Promethion High-Definition Multiplexed Respirometry Cages (from Sable Systems International) on a 1 week on, 3 weeks off cycle until death or study termination (~1.5 years after study initiation).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

source: To eliminate the stress of acclimatizing to the metabolic cage as a potential confounder, we dropped the first 24 hr of data (empirically we observed that mice reached a steady state after the first light cycle).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing data processing.

claim: 77 runs were removed for being too short (2.2%).
source: We removed 77 runs for being too short (2.2%).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing quality control.

source: We removed 295 runs (~8.4%) for having too many outlier timepoints.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing quality control.

claim: No imputation of any data points was done.
source: Data points which were flagged as outliers were censored, thus, no imputation of any data points was done.

claim: The study trained a discrete state HMM on the data after QC and outlier detection to identify common activity states and assign timepoints to these states.
source: In order to identify common activity states and assign timepoints to these states, we trained a discrete state HMM on the data after QC and outlier detection.

claim: The dataset was split into a training set of 2689 runs and a held-out validation set of 471 runs to determine the number of HMM activity states.
source: In order to determine the number of HMM activity states, we split the dataset into a training set of 2689 runs and a held-out a validation set of 471 runs.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing model training.

claim: The selection process yielded 6 as the optimal number of states.
source: This selection process yielded 6 as the optimal number of states, we then fit a final robust HMM using all the data with 6 states.

claim: The study controlled for exposure to the phenotyping cage as a confounder using ANOVA/multiple linear regression.
source: We controlled for exposure to the phenotyping cage as a confounder using ANOVA/multiple linear regression.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing data processing.

claim: The study normalized each gas measurement to the mean body mass across all runs (31 g).
source: We then normalized each gas measurement to the mean body mass across all runs (31 g).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing normalization.

claim: The study fit age-specific phenotype networks using 3-month age bins starting from age 0 as separate age bins.
source: We fit age-specific phenotype networks using taking 3-month age bins starting from age 0 as separate age bins.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing network analysis.

claim: The study used a variant of the graphical LASSO called time-varying graphical LASSO which fits a separate model per age bin but penalizes differences between adjacent age bins.
source: In order to account for changes in relationships between features as mice age, we used a variant of the graphical LASSO called time-varying graphical LASSO (Hallac et al., 2017) which fits a separate model per age bin but penalizes differences between adjacent age bins (to encode our prior that changes in network connectivity occur gradually with age).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing network analysis.

claim: The study adopted the nonparanormal covariance estimator because several features are non-Gaussian in distribution.
source: Since several of our features are non-Gaussian in distribution, we adopted the nonparanormal covariance estimator described in Liu et al., 2009.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing network analysis.

claim: The study bootstrap sampled the estimated graphical model 1000 times and consensus clustered features using spectral clustering.
source: In order to cluster features into phenotype clusters, we bootstrap sample the estimated graphical model 1000 times and consensus cluster (Monti et al., 2003) features using spectral clustering.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing clustering.

claim: The study collected tail clippings and extracted DNA from all animals, which were genotyped using the 143,259-probe GigaMUGA array from the Illumina Infinium II platform by NeoGen Corp.
source: We collected tail clippings and extracted DNA from all animals. Samples were genotyped using the 143,259-probe GigaMUGA array from the Illumina Infinium II platform (Morgan et al., 2015) by NeoGen Corp. (genomics.neogen.com/).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing genotyping.

claim: After filtering genetic markers for uniquely mapped probes, genotype quality, and a 20% genotype missingness threshold, the dataset contained 116,377 markers.
source: After filtering genetic markers for uniquely mapped probes, genotype quality, and a 20% genotype missingness threshold, our dataset contained 116,377 markers.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing genotype processing.

claim: For each mouse, the study inferred the founders-of-origin for each of the alleles at each marker using the R package: qtl2.
source: For each mouse, starting with its genotypes at the 116,377 markers and the genotypes of the eight founder strains at the same markers, we inferred the founders-of-origin for each of the alleles at each marker using the R package: qtl2 (Broman et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing genetic analysis.

claim: For each of the 309 derived phenotypes, the study computed the heritability using a custom implementation of EMMA, a standard linear mixed model used for genetic association analyses.
source: For each of the 309 derived phenotypes in this study, we computed the heritability (proportion of phenotypic variance explained by additive genetic effects, or PVE) using a custom implementation of EMMA (Kang et al., 2008), a standard linear mixed model used for genetic association analyses.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing heritability analysis.

claim: For the 45 phenotypes with significant nonzero heritability, the study computed genetic correlation for each pair of phenotypes using a matrix-variate linear mixed model, while conditioning on the fixed effects of age and cohort.
source: For the 45 phenotypes with significant nonzero heritability, we compute genetic correlation for each pair of phenotypes, using a matrix-variate linear mixed model (Furlotte and Eskin, 2015), while conditioning on the fixed effects of age and cohort.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing genetic correlation analysis.
